newsitem.title: USA: Nike has $3.5 bln in orders through January.
newsitem.headline: Nike has $3.5 bln in orders through January.

text.p: Nike Inc has $3.5 billion worth of orders for its athletic footwear and apparel for delivery through January, an official said.

That order volume represents about a 66 percent gain over orders at a similar time last year, said Rick Anguilla, director of investor relations. The surge partly reflects a growing retail practice to place orders for future delivery.

Anguilla, who spoke at the Montgomery Securities Investment Conference, reiterated afterward that Nike is comfortable with analysts' predictions that its sales and earnings will grow about 15 percent annually through 2001.

Asked if the company had sufficient inventories to meet demand, Anguilla said "The systems are definitely being taxed," but Nike is "completely comfortable" with its ability to meet demand with the inventory supply and replenishment systems in place.

Nike footwear -- which grew sales at 20 percent last year, about double analysts' estimates for the industry as a whole -- should continue its growth pace, said Elizabeth Dolan, vice president of marketing.
"Footwear is a $4.4 billion business for us this year," Dolan said. "We believe that, despite the dramatic growth of the past two years, we can sustain it," she said.
Dolan also said Nike sees growth in its overall business.
"Nike is a growth company because sports is a growth industry," she said. Nike sales grew 34 percent last year.
